assets.density: dense closed-canopy baseline for later sparse woodland
assets.prompt:
Image1 is the EXACT current tile to retouch. Image2 is the approved grass-ground color/texture reference. Image3 is a COMMON TREE-SCALE/FAMILY reference only: its medium rounded crowns are closer to the desired common size; do not copy its mountains or composition.
Use case: precise-object-edit. Retouch this SAME opaque forest terrain tile. Keep the original terrain forms and all principal rounded hilltops/rocky mountain peaks, their positions, heights and proportions, the shared grass base, upright viewing direction, mature deciduous tree family and existing rich natural palette. The FOREST INTERIOR MUST REMAIN DENSE AND CLOSED; this is not sparse woodland.
CHANGE1—NATURAL FOREST EDGE. Remove the long straight/chamfered forest-wall runs and its implied six-sided outline. The main canopy outline must be genuinely irregular, scalloped by a few substantial tree-crown groups, with several unequal shallow recesses and little lobes. Around that main edge paint a6-12pixel-wide-at210px organic transition of LOW UNDERSTORY: bushes, saplings, low foliage and fading ground cover, with patches of the same grass background showing BETWEEN and THROUGH it. Include2-4 narrow irregular grass fingers entering the peripheral understory to different shallow depths, WITHOUT opening up or thinning the dense center. Main tall crowns stop in different places behind this low growth; there must be no continuous dark forest wall, cutout contour, pale outline, hexagonal band, smooth circular rim or equally spaced decorative shrub border. Individual crowns/shrubs end naturally. Ground, roots, bushes and grass must be painted as one integrated landscape, with a gradual reduction in vegetation density at the edge, NOT merely an airbrushed fog/blur halo.
CHANGE2—CONSISTENT TREE SCALE. All regular mature crowns in this set must have approximately the SAME medium size: typical full crown diameter28-32pixels in a210pixel square, with a natural range24-36pixels, roughly14percent of the tile width. Foreground trees only slightly larger than distant trees, not giant trees. Trunks and foliage scale must match on plains/hills/mountains. Adjust the NUMBER of crowns as necessary to keep the original dense coverage while using that common size. Keep a few large coherent connected foliage masses, not a stippled scattering of miniature trees. Broad simple crown light/midtone/shadow volumes, low leaf detail, no tiny white sparkle texture. Important: keep ridge/summit silhouettes clean and clear, and only the low peripheral understory/background blend soft. No global blur, pastel desaturation, brighter lime saturation, flat vector or plastic CGI.
All meaningful vegetation, tips, trunks, shadows and relief remain COMPLETE INSIDE the full source-orientation regular hex; use only a narrow varied grass skirt. Shape the new irregular edge inward within the existing safe footprint—do not enlarge it outside the hex. Foreground grass can be visible under the low understory but there should not be a wide vacant moat. Background fills the full square opaquely. No visible hex guide, border, frame, UI, labels, watermark or transparency.
PLAIN FOREST: keep genuinely flat ground with no hills or rocks. Its current individual crowns are too big: reduce them to the common medium scale and add overlapping crowns to preserve a densely closed stand. Do not preserve the current giant-tree scale.
Pointy-top hex vertices in210square: (105,0),(195.93,52.5),(195.93,157.5),(105,210),(14.07,157.5),(14.07,52.5). Do not trace those sides with the forest edge: they only define the outer maximum limit.
